title: Millions in prisoner funds missing at women’s correctional
content:
Government corruption is not sparing persons deprived of liberty (PDL), it seems.

Rights group Karapatan said that up to ₱6 million of funds remitted by families of Correctional Institution for Women (CIW) PDL for personal use have gone missing.

A recent audit revealed that out of the total recorded remittances of ₱13 million, only ₱7 million could be accounted for by Bureau of Corrections (Bucor) personnel handling the “trust fund,” Karapatan said.

Monies sent by families are deposited in a “trust fund” handled by CIW personnel from which the PDLs can withdraw a minimal amount weekly.

Karapatan said that CIW Superintendent Daisy Castillote refuses to hold concerned personnel accountable, offering instead to have the missing amount replaced using funds earned from the PDLs’ telephone calls, which currently cost ₱3.00 every five minutes.

Castillote reportedly plans to raise the fee of each five-minute telephone call to ₱5.00 until the funds ‘lost’ are replenished.

“On top of this, the PDLs will no longer be receiving a share from the telephone call income that they could use to defray costs for their dormitories’ needs,” Karapatan in a statement said.

The prison manager’s so-called solution has angered the political prisoners and other PDLs who said that the prisoners should not be made to bear the burden of replacing the missing funds, Karapatan added.

title: 19 die in floods, landslides
content:
The southwest monsoon-battered country suffered 19 casualties and 1.3 million affected residents in large swathes of the country, the Office of Civil Defense (OCD) reported on Tuesday, August 11. Enhanced by typhoons Luis and Maymay, the monsoon dumped a month’s worth of rain in the affected regions in the last ten days.

Authorities said 384,520 families were affected across 10 regions, namely Metro Manila, Cordillera, Ilocos, Cagayan Valley, Central Luzon, Calabarzon, Mimaropa, Bicol, Western Visayas and Zamboanga peninsula as of Monday.

Benguet Province recorded the most number of fatalities with 12 due to three separate landslides in La Trinidad (2), Baguio (9) and Atok (1). In Baguio, three were rescued while one remains missing, local police reported.

Two persons were also reported killed by a rockslide in Rodriguez, Rizal Province located immediately east of Metro Manila, one died after being struck by a falling tree in Antipolo City and another drowned in Binangonan.

In Batangas Province, one died of electrocution in Lipa City when he touched an electric pole while fording a flooded street; another was killed in Santa Teresita, Batangas due to a landslide; and one drowned in Batangas City due to drowning.

title: Tuta ng US ang ama noon, ganoon rin ba ang anak ngayon?
content:
Tuwang-tuwa ang gubyerno ng Estados Unidos kay Pangulong Ferdinand Marcos Sr. noon, sa kabila ng karahasan sa mamamayan at nakawan sa kaban ng bayan ng kanyang diktadura.

Si Ferdinand Marcos Jr. kaya? Naiiba ba sa kanyang ama o pareho lang sila?

Pakinggan kung ano ang naganap noon at ihambing sa nagaganap ngayon, dito sa ika-19 sa serye ng maigsing dramang panradyo na unang inilabas ng Kodao noong 2001.

Muling inilalathala ito sa gitna na tumitinding presensiya ng militar ng US sa bansang Pilipinas bukod pa sa ibang pakana ng US tulad ng Pax Silica.

author: Kodao Productions
title: Sino ang tunay na terorista?
content:
Ang Saudi na si Osama bin Laden – dating tauhan mismo ng US – ang may pakana ng atakeng 9/11 sa New York, subalit ang mamamayang Afghan ang pinagbayad ng daang libong buhay ng Estados Unidos.

Pakinggan ang krimen ng Estados Unidos sa ibang bansa, dito sa ika-18 sa serye ng maigsing dramang panradyo na unang inilabas ng Kodao noong 2001.

Muling inilalathala ito sa gitna na tumitinding presensiya ng militar ng US sa bansang Pilipinas na nagbabadya ng ibayong karahasang militar sa ating bahagi ng mundo.

title: Pax Silica: From Obscurity to National Scrutiny and Why Marcos and Trump are Losing
content:
By Renato Reyes, Jr. / President, Bagong Alyansang Makabayan

In April this year, when we first learned of the Philippines joining the Pax Silica initiative and the establishment of an economic zone in Luzon, public engagement on the issue was confined to the usual activist circles. It wasn’t the hottest topic in town, and the concepts of imperialist war, plunder, and greed were not yet thoroughly exposed.

It is now August, nearly four months since the Philippines joined the initiative, and in that short period of time, Pax Silica has become one of the most talked-about issues, next to the impeachment trial of Sara Duterte. It has become a staple of news programs, commentaries, and, of course, protest actions. From relative obscurity, it is now the subject of national scrutiny. The public uproar was so loud that Malacañang had to hold a press briefing with the BCDA (Bases Conversion Development Authority) to debunk the so-called myths about Pax Silica — which were actually the valid concerns of the people regarding the economic zone.

What changed in the last four months?

The Pax Silica narrative of “development” and “technological innovation” collided with the harsh realities of a semi-feudal and semi-colonial Philippines. title: SC junks bids to halt Sara’s impeachment hearings
content:
The Supreme Court (SC) dismissed consolidated petitions filed by Vice President Sara Duterte and lawyer Israelito Torreon seeking to halt impeachment proceedings by the House of Representatives (HOR). The High Court ruled the case moot because the HOR had long concluded the proceedings and the impeachment trial by the Senate had in fact been ongoing for exactly a month already.

In separate pleadings, Duterte and her supporters led by Torreon asked the SC to issue cease orders against the HOR in March and April, respectively. They said the HOR Justice Committee exceeded its power during the initial hearings and evidence gathering.

In its en banc session today, the SC said the petitions no longer required resolution, allowing the Senate to continue the ongoing trial.

The SC explained that the House’s transmittal of the Articles of Impeachment marked the end of the House’s role in the impeachment process and the initiation of the impeachment case. As a result, the actions the petitioner sought to stop had already been completed.

Bicol Saro Rep. Terry Ridon, one of the 11 public prosecutors in the impeachment case, was quick to welcome the Court’s decision, saying the Justice Committee had been affirmed and vindicated.

“With this decision, all talk about the ‘mini-trial’ and ‘fishing expedition’ that the Vice President’s camp has repeatedly promoted is over,” Ridon said.

title: Noms de ‘chichirya’ ni Sara
content:
It doesn’t need a pedant or linguist to understand that the hundreds of the so-called informers of Sara Zimmerman Duterte Carpio who profited from her munificence are a work of fiction, and the names used are not only “chichirya” brands but are also the products of the very fertile imagination marinated with beer and scotch in some comedy bar. The informer production machine was such in great rush to fool the government, the Commission on Audit (COA) and the taxpaying public that they had to resort to the use of weird names to hide the real beneficiaries.

Aside from concentrating on Piattos, Tempura, Nova, Oishi and a gaggle of junk food brands, the masterminds of the image and moniker fabrication also deliberately limited their documents to authenticate the receipt of cash, food and medicines to more than 800 acknowledgment receipts (ARs) that the defense now wishes to do away with, raising the issue of genuineness of the marked documents. Weren’t the defense and prosecution involved in such marking? It seems the defense is deathly scared of being drowned by the confirmation of witnesses that Sara did not submit the receipts, confirmation of identities of recipients and proof that the purchased pieces off information were true and helped both the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) achieve their goals.

title: Did the Pasig Court Bypass the Labor Code?
content:
On July 9, National Capital Region’s (NCR) Regional Tripartite Wage and Productivity Board (RTWPB) announced that the first tranche of its Wage Order No. 27 would take effect on July 25. It grants a PHP 60 daily wage increase, followed by an additional P25 on January 20 next year, raising the minimum daily wage for non-agricultural workers in Metro Manila to P780.

The cumulative P85 increase is RTWPB’s largest single wage adjustment since its creation in 1989. While welcomed by most workers, however, the amount to them still falls far short of a living wage.

But even a mandated increase, it seems, is difficult for workers to receive. Before the wage hike could even fully take effect, its implementation was put on hold on the eve of the day most workers expect their monthly salaries.

Pasig Regional Trial Court (RTC) branch 152 issued a Temporary Restraining Order (TRO) against the latest wage order last July 30, upon petition by two construction companies with at least hundreds of employees and billions of pesos in cumulative government infrastructure contracts.

Readycon Trading and Construction Corp., and R-II Builders, Inc. claimed the wage order would cause “grave injustice and irreparable injury” to their lucrative business, seeking relief from the Court against the alleged adverse effects of the wage order on their rights as businesses. title: NDFP: Marcos GRP’s claim of openness to talks resumption, ‘empty, unconvincing’
content:
The National Democratic Front of the Philippines (NDFP) Negotiating Panel challenged the Ferdinand Marcos Jr. government to prove sincerity beyond claims of openness to resuming peace negotiations.

NDFP chief negotiator Julie de Lima said Office of the Presidential Adviser on Peace, Reunification and Unity secretary Mel Senen Sarmiento’s statement that the Marcos government is open to resuming talks with the CPP-NPA-NDF[P] (Communist Party of the Philippines-New People’s Army-NDFP) “must now be tested through concrete action.”

“After decades of military offensives which have failed to meet its supposed aim of ending the NPA, relentless terror-tagging by the NTF-Elcac (National Task Force to End Local Communist Armed Conflict) and senior officials of the GRP (Government of the Republic of the Philippines), and  widespread killings of NDFP peace consultants, the GRP cannot simply invoke the language of peace while continuing policies that undermine the very conditions needed for the meaningful resumption of the peace negotiations,” de Lima said.

In a press briefing on Friday to mark his first 100 days in office, Sarmiento said negotiations with the revolutionary Left may be resumed, “provided both sides are sincere about achieving lasting peace and have no ‘hidden agenda.’”

title: Palpak na propaganda ni Sara
content:
Kung sinuman ang nagbibigay-payo kay Sara Zimmerman Duterte Carpio ay nararapat nang umalma at pagsabihan ang kanilang alaga na lalong lumalabo ang kanyang tindig sa kasong impeachment sa Senado dahil sa kanyang mga binibitawan sa The Hague at maging dito sa bansa. Ayon nga sa mga bihasa sa batas, nakaririmarim ang mga pahayag ni Sara, lalo pa nang pagbintangan niya ang International Criminal Court (ICC) na tuta bi Pangulong Ferdinand Marcos Jr. at ni dating Senador Antonio Trillanes IV.

Maaaring pinalakpakan siya sa pulutong ng mga Pilipinong nasa The Hague subalit parang sinampal niya ang 181 bansa na nagtataguyod ng hukumang ito na itinatag batay sa Rome Statute. Mabilisan din naming tinanggihan ng ICC ang paratang at sinabing ito as “fair” at kumikilos nang walang kinikilangan, at tanging Rome Statute at international law ang batayan ng mga proseso nito, mula sa paghahain ng mga asuntong “crime against humanity” hanggang sa pag-uusig at pagdinig ng mga hukom sa mga argumento ng umuusig at nagtatanggol.

Sapagkat hindi rin naman kilala na palabasa itong si Sara at maaaring buga lang nang buga na parang si Donald Trump na ang IQ ay 73, hindi nakapagtataka na puro kapalpakan ang namumutawi sa kanyang bibig. Gaya nang bigkasin niya na hihintayin ang paglabas ng kanyang ama mula sa kulungan sa loob ng isang linggo. Puspos ng pagtanggi na sinabi niya ito. Ganoon din ang nangyari
